newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Officials say U.S. may announce NATO choices soon.
newsitem.headline: Officials say U.S. may announce NATO choices soon.

text.p: U.S. officials said on Thursday they expected the United States to decide and announce within days whether it will press to limit initial NATO enlargement to three East European states or support a larger number.

"I expect a decision very shortly," U.S. Defence Undersecretary Walter Slocombe said, noting that President Bill Clinton met senior members of the Senate in Washington on Wednesday night to discuss the controversial issue.

The Senate, like other NATO members' parliaments, would have to approve any expansion agreement. Some key lawmakers have questioned whether the alliance should be expanded at all because of costs and doubts about would-be members' military readiness.
France and some other European allies are pressing NATO leaders to invite Romania and Slovenia as well as front-runners Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic at a summit in Madrid early next month.

U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen told reporters who trevelled with him to a two-day meeting of alliance defence ministers in Brussels that he personally felt "smaller would be better" in the first round of invitations.
Cohen and other U.S. officials, who asked not to be identified, said that a U.S. decision could come before the end of the week.

"Obviously there is support on the part of the Europeans for Romania and Slovenia," said Cohen, but he stressed that the alliance must remain cohesive. He raised questions about costs, the military adaptability of would-be members and Senate reluctance.

"No matter what happens in Madrid, the next step is to persuade the Senate to ratify it," he said, urging Western leaders to make clear in Madrid that additional membership rounds would follow the initial invitations.

The U.S. ambassador to NATO, Robert Hunter, told reporters that the alliance planned a public announcement on membership in advance of the summit to ensure there were no surprises at the meeting, being held on July 8-9.
"We are not looking for an Oscar night," Hunter told a press conference with Slocombe.
"The hope and plan is that NATO itself will come to a (public) conclusion a bit in front of Madrid so that everyone will know what to expect at the summit."
He stressed that the first round of invitations would not be the last despite fears from aspiring countries that they may be left out of the alliance.
"It is the clear commitment of the entire alliance that there will a be progressive admission of countries," Hunter stressed. "So yes, more countries will get in."
